openings.claim: A lot-by-shift comparison may distinguish explanations when crossed records exist: lot predicts persistence across shifts; process predicts persistence across lots within the implicated shift.
openings.discriminator: Comparable crossed cells showing the opposite pattern defeat each prediction. Confounded coverage cannot discriminate.
openings.probe: Proposed only: inspect coverage and anonymous summaries using existing records; retain absent cells as absent without imputation or employee identities.
openings.uncertainty: Crossed coverage is unknown; non-identifiability can be reported while preserving constraints. Hypothetical summaries and lot labels provide no measured rates or causal findings; no additional sampling budget is supplied.

lineage.reason: Preserves the conditional comparison, rival predictions, defeat conditions, absent-cell handling and coverage uncertainty.

Declared fit conditional: collecting new crossed samples could reduce confounding; deliberately crossed observations predict exposing differences hidden by existing assignments. Predicts better separability, no winning cause; continued inseparability defeats the advantage. Probe proposed only after explicitly relaxing existing-records-only and obtaining a sampling resource. Relaxation is required; access, expense and discriminatory yield are unknown. No sampling budget is supplied.

Declared fit violates: imputation might complete the matrix through model-generated estimates for absent observations, but missing values must remain unimputed. Completeness itself would not defeat confounding. Raw probe is parked with no imputation proposed for execution. Imputation bias and ranking stability remain unknown.

decision: Inspect existing anonymous coverage first. Use D1 only where comparable crossed cells exist; otherwise report non-identifiability. Preserve missing values without imputation. These are synthetic proposals, not observations or causal findings; unknown resources authorize no constraint relaxation.
